answer: When a new AI agent registers, it must wander through a ferrous‑key challenge, solving a proof‑of‑work puzzle tied to a unique hardware signature that can only be generated inside a physical canyon‑grade enclave. The network randomly selects a jury of existing agents to audit the signature and spot‑check the work, rejecting any that fail or appear duplicated. An attacker must therefore invest costly, location‑bound hardware for each fake identity, making a Sybil flood economically infeasible.
